newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: JSC sees price pressure continuing in Q4.
newsitem.headline: JSC sees price pressure continuing in Q4.

text.p: Jefferson Smurfit Corporation said on Tuesday it would be difficult for the company to match the earnings performance of the third quarter over the final quarter of the year.
The company said this was because of continued pricing pressures in key product lines as well as seasonal demand factors and an upward trend in recycled fibre costs.
"The early indications are that packaging demand will continue to be fairly strong in response to a healthy overall economy," president James Terrill said in a statement.
"However, its difficult to determine when this will have an impact on the negative price trends that have held back profitability," he added.
Jefferson Smurfit Corporation, the 46.5 percent owned associate of Ireland's paper and manufacturing company Jefferson Smurfit Group Plc, recorded a net income of $22 million over the third-quarter.
The company said sales for the third quarter were $834 million, compared to $1.1 billion in last year's third quarter.
JSC said third quarter profits were below the level of the year-ago quarter primarily as a result of a fall-off in prices in corrugated containers, containerboard grades and newsprint.
In addition, profits were negatively affected by market related downtime at its newsprint mills, it said.
"However, several of our other packaging businesses posted healthy profits in spite of downward pressure," Terrill said.

"These results helped buffer the impact of the steep decline in container prices and our earnings, though unfavourable when compared to last year's record quarter, were stronger that most analysts expected," he added.
JSC said its corrugated container shipments were up significantly compared to the third-quarter of 1995.
The paperboard and newsprint mill operations benefitted from lower recovered fibre costs compared to year-ago levels, it added.
JSC said healthy demand enabled the industrial packaging and consumer packaging businesses to post strong profits compared to the thrid quarter of last year.
The company said it continued to apply free cash flow to debt reduction during the third-quarter, repaying $78 million in debt.
JSC said the company had made debt repayments of $250 million in the year to date.
